questions.stem: In paper chromatography, why must the pencil line with the sample spot be drawn above the solvent level?

options.text: Because the pencil line would dissolve in the solvent
So that the sample does not dissolve directly into the solvent before it can be separated
Because the solvent needs to flow downwards

questions.explanation: If the sample spot is below the solvent level, the substances would dissolve directly into the solvent rather than being carried up the paper by the rising solvent. The spot must be above the solvent so that the solvent rises through it, separating the components.

questions.stem: A student wants to obtain pure water from salt water. Which method should they use?
questions.explanation: Simple distillation is used to recover the liquid (water) from a solution. The water evaporates, passes through a condenser where it cools back to liquid, and is collected as pure distillate. Evaporation would only recover the salt, not the water.
